# PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER

## Scope of this Part

## 69.1

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.1] (1) This Part contains provisions about the court’s power to appoint a receiver.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.1] (2) In this Part ‘receiver’ includes a manager.

## Court’s power to appoint receiver

## 69.2

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (1) The court may appoint a receiver –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (a) before proceedings have started;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (b) in existing proceedings; or

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (c) on or after judgment.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (2) A receiver must be an individual.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (3) The court may at any time –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (a) terminate the appointment of a receiver; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (b) appoint another receiver in his place.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.2] (Practice Direction 69 describes the powers for the court to appoint a receiver.)

## How to apply for the appointment of a receiver

## 69.3

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.3] An application for the appointment of a receiver –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.3] (a) may be made without notice ; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.3] (b) must be supported by written evidence.

## Service of order appointing receiver

## 69.4

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.4] An order appointing a receiver must be served by the party who applied for it on –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.4] (a) the person appointed as receiver;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.4] (b) unless the court orders otherwise, every other party to the proceedings; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.4] (c) such other persons as the court may direct.

## Security

## 69.5

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (1) The court may direct that before a receiver begins to act or within a specified time he must either –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (a) give such security as the court may determine; or

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (b) file and serve on all parties to the proceedings evidence that he already has in force sufficient security,

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] to cover his liability for his acts and omissions as a receiver.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (2) The court may terminate the appointment of the receiver if he fails to –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (a) give the security; or

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] (b) satisfy the court as to the security he has in force,

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.5] by the date specified.

## Receiver’s application for directions

## 69.6

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.6] (1) The receiver may apply to the court at any time for directions to assist him in carrying out his function as a receiver.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.6] (2) The court, when it gives directions, may also direct the receiver to serve on any person –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.6] (a) the directions; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.6] (b) the application for directions.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.6] (Practice Direction 69 makes provision for the form of applications by, and directions to, a receiver.)

## Receiver’s remuneration

## 69.7

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (1) A receiver may only charge for his services if the court –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (a) so directs; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (b) specifies the basis on which the receiver is to be remunerated.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (2) The court may specify –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (a) who is to be responsible for paying the receiver; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (b) the fund or property from which the receiver is to recover his remuneration.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (3) If the court directs that the amount of a receiver’s remuneration is to be determined by the court –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (a) the receiver may not recover any remuneration for his services without a determination by the court; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (b) the receiver or any party may apply at any time for such a determination to take place.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (4) Unless the court orders otherwise, in determining the remuneration of a receiver the court shall award such sum as is reasonable and proportionate in all the circumstances and which takes into account –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (a) the time properly given by him and his staff to the receivership;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (b) the complexity of the receivership;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (c) any responsibility of an exceptional kind or degree which falls on the receiver in consequence of the receivership;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (d) the effectiveness with which the receiver appears to be carrying out, or to have carried out, his duties; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (e) the value and nature of the subject matter of the receivership.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.7] (5) The court may refer the determination of a receiver’s remuneration to a costs judge.

## Accounts

## 69.8

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (1) The court may order a receiver to prepare and serve accounts.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (Practice Direction 69 contains provisions about directions for the preparation and service of accounts.)

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (2) A party served with such accounts may apply for an order permitting him to inspect any document in the possession of the receiver relevant to those accounts.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (3) Any party may, within 14 days of being served with the accounts, serve notice on the receiver –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (a) specifying any item in the accounts to which he objects;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (b) giving the reason for such objection; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (c) requiring the receiver, within 14 days of receipt of the notice, either –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (i) to notify all the parties who were served with the accounts that he accepts the objection; or

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (ii) if he does not accept the objection, to apply for an examination of the accounts in relation to the contested item.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (4) When the receiver applies for the examination of the accounts he must at the same time file –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (a) the accounts; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (b) a copy of the notice served on him under this rule.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (5) If the receiver fails to comply with paragraph (3)(c) of this rule, any party may apply to the court for an examination of the accounts in relation to the contested item.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (6) At the conclusion of its examination of the accounts the court will certify the result.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.8] (Practice Direction 40A provides for inquiries into accounts.)

## Non-compliance by receiver

## 69.9

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (1) If a receiver fails to comply with any rule, practice direction or direction of the court the court may order him to attend a hearing to explain his non-compliance.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (2) At the hearing the court may make any order it considers appropriate, including –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (a) terminating the appointment of the receiver;

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (b) reducing the receiver’s remuneration or disallowing it altogether; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (c) ordering the receiver to pay the costs of any party.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (3) Where –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (a) the court has ordered a receiver to pay a sum of money into court; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] (b) the receiver has failed to do so,

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.9] the court may order him to pay interest on that sum for the time he is in default at such rate as it considers appropriate.

## Application for discharge of receiver

## 69.10

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.10] (1) A receiver or any party may apply for the receiver to be discharged on completion of his duties.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.10] (2) The application notice must be served on the persons who were required under rule 69.4 to be served with the order appointing the receiver.

## Order discharging or terminating appointment of receiver

## 69.11

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.11] (1) An order discharging or terminating the appointment of a receiver may –

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.11] (a) require him to pay into court any money held by him; or

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.11] (b) specify the person to whom he must pay any money or transfer any assets still in his possession; and

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.11] (c) make provision for the discharge or cancellation of any guarantee given by the receiver as security.

[PART 69 – COURT’S POWER TO APPOINT A RECEIVER > 69.11] (2) The order must be served on the persons who were required under rule 69.4 to be served with the order appointing the receiver.
